text:
Rae: heads-up: canary warmup is stalling on some bundles that were published with compression. pattern: lots of small `Range` 206s and post-decompress checksum failures, no OOM.
toaster-bot: [warmup] event=range_retry_spike model=seq2seq-large shard=sh-42
Ben: paste a minimal log?
Rae: here->
```
2026-05-05T10:02:01Z loader fetch range 0-65535 -> 206
2026-05-05T10:02:01Z loader decompress -> error: truncated input
2026-05-05T10:02:01Z verify_post_decompress expected=aa11bb got=000000
2026-05-05T10:02:02Z retry attempt=1 backoff=40ms
```
Isha: seems like header/deflate state got split across ranges. We currently verify the decompressed safetensors bytes which fails if the stream is invalid.
Ben: quick options: (1) bump initial prime to N bytes to capture headers (easy, wastes bandwidth), (2) on checksum fail try a single "header-probe" larger read (elastic header-probe), (3) rely on manifest-stored compressed digest to verify compressed bytes before decompress.
Rae: I tried (2) in a micro-canary: elastic header-probe (512k) fixed the stalls in most cases and small shards didn't see much impact.
Isha: API/abstraction question: should the loader expose compression metadata to the runtime or hide it completely? I'm leaning toward exposing compression.type and compression.digest to help observability.
Ben: agreed. Proposal for manifest v2 compression block:
- compression.type: "gzip" | "brotli" | "none"
- compression.digest_sha256: optional
- compression.index_url: optional (sidecar that lists per-chunk digests)
If digest present loader verifies compressed bytes first and skips elastic header-probe.
Rae: add metrics: `loader.compressed_verify_fail`, `loader.elastic_header_probes`, `loader.compression_type_seen` (counts by type). Tag with `model`, `shard`, `region`, `canary`.
Isha: retry/backoff policy: exponential backoff w/ jitter for range reads, max 3 attempts. On checksum mismatch escalate to elastic header-probe once, then full-object fetch if that fails.
Ben: storage note: CDNs sometimes re-chunk responses which can defeat byte-range assumptions. compressed_digest is only reliable if CDN preserves object bytes; sidecar index helps with rechunking since it validates chunk-by-chunk.
Rae: test plan: unit tests for partial compressed streams, an integration harness that serves split-range responses for gzip and brotli, and e2e canary with synthetic compressed bundles. Also add a stress test against our CDN staging to ensure chunking doesn't make it worse.
Isha: long-term idea: introduce a compact sidecar index at publish time that contains small chunk digests so loader can validate subranges cheaply. That requires publisher tooling and backwards-compat semantics; we should spec it in the RFC.
Ben: owner split: Isha -> manifest schema PR + metrics; Ben -> loader changes: elastic header-probe, compressed-verify path, telemetry; Kai -> storage/CDN guidance + test harness. Rae -> open RFC follow-up and create rollout checklist.
Rae: created ticket INF-10011 "elastic header-probe + manifest compressed digest + sidecar index" and linked initial canary logs in the ticket.
Kai: I'll mock CDN re-chunking in the testbed and add a failing-case scenario.
Ben: I'll push a small feature flag so we can gate elastic header-probe on canary.
Isha: I'll include example manifests and compatibility notes in the PR.
Rae: thanks all 69a3fb4aa. If canary shows regressions we revert the flag.
